# Design System — components (brand: acme)
> GENERATED by @ds/context — DO NOT EDIT. Source hash sha256:40eab412d89cd909. Regenerate: pnpm --filter @ds/context build

This system is closed-world: every legal component is enumerated in registries/components-index.json and every legal token in registries/tokens-index.json. Anything not in those registries is provably fabricated — do not emit it.

All 21 exports below come from `@ds/react` (the only public entry point). Props tables are generated from the code registry and are exact — including literal-union types.

## Alert

Import: `import { Alert } from '@ds/react';`

Static status message rendered as a plain `<div>` with a tone-mapped ARIA role: interruptive tones (`danger`, `warning`) use `role="alert"` so assistive technology announces them immediately; calm tones (`info`, `success`) use the polite `role="status"`. For permanent, static content (a danger-zone explainer, a standing notice) pass `isLive={false}` to keep the tone styling while dropping the live-region role entirely, so the message is not re-announced on every page load. Tones follow the soft recipe — status surface background, status border, status text — through the `--ds-alert-*` component hooks, with a decorative tone icon. An optional dismiss control (react-aria-components `Button` internally) appears when `onDismiss` is provided; the caller owns removing the alert.

Static component (no react-aria-components base) — plain semantic HTML.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Plain string only; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `isLive` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Whether the alert is a live region that assistive technology announces when it appears. When `true` (default), the tone decides the ARIA role (`alert` for `danger`/`warning`, `status` for `info`/`success`). Set to `false` for permanent, static content — e.g. a danger-zone explainer that is part of the page rather than a notification — so the message is NOT re-announced on every load: the alert then renders as a plain `<div>` with the tone styling and no live-region role at all. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | no | — | When provided, the alert renders a dismiss control (an icon-only accessible button labeled "Dismiss") and calls this handler when it is pressed. The alert does not remove itself — the caller owns visibility. |
| `title` | `string` | no | — | Optional bold heading line rendered above the message. Replaces the native HTML tooltip attribute of the same name — it is rendered as visible text, never as a tooltip. |
| `tone` | `"info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger"` | no | `'info'` | Status intent of the alert. Soft recipe: each tone pairs a status surface background with its matching status border and text colors — never a solid fill. While the alert is live (see `isLive`), the tone also decides the ARIA role: `danger` and `warning` are interruptive and render `role="alert"`; `info` and `success` render the polite `role="status"`. |

Theming hooks: `--ds-alert-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Alert>Your changes were saved as a draft.</Alert>
<Alert tone="success" title="Deployed">Build 42 is live.</Alert>
<Alert tone="danger" onDismiss={() => setVisible(false)}>
  Payment failed — check your card details.
</Alert>
<Alert tone="danger" isLive={false} title="Danger zone">
  Deleting the workspace permanently removes all projects.
</Alert>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/Alert/Alert.stories.tsx`

## Badge

Import: `import { Badge } from '@ds/react';`

Static status label rendered as a plain `<span>`. Purely presentational: no interaction, no focus, no ARIA role beyond the text itself. Tones use the soft recipe — a `*-surface` background with the matching `*-text` foreground via the `--ds-badge-*` component hooks.

Static component (no react-aria-components base) — plain semantic HTML.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Plain string only; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `tone` | `"info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| "neutral"` | no | `'neutral'` | Status intent of the badge. `neutral` is a plain label, `info` an informational note, `success` a positive state, `warning` a caution, `danger` an error or destructive state. Soft recipe: each tone pairs a status surface background with its matching status text color — never a solid fill. |

Theming hooks: `--ds-badge-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Badge>Draft</Badge>
<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger">Failed</Badge>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/Badge/Badge.stories.tsx`

## Button

Import: `import { Button } from '@ds/react';`

Accessible push button built on react-aria-components `Button`. Keyboard behavior, focus management, and press semantics come from React Aria; visual states are driven purely by RAC data attributes (`data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`, `data-pending`) and `--ds-*` tokens.

Built on react-aria-components `Button`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `Button` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `isLoading` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Marks the button as busy with an in-progress action: interaction is disabled, the state is announced to assistive technology, and a CSS-only spinner is shown before the label. The label stays visible. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | `'md'` | Control size. Maps to the `--ds-size-control-*` height scale. |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost"` | no | `'primary'` | Visual intent of the button. `primary` is the single main action of a view, `secondary` a supporting action, `ghost` a low-emphasis inline action, `danger` a destructive action. |

Inherited-but-legal `Button` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `autoFocus: boolean`, `isDisabled: boolean`, `name: string`, `onPress: (e: PressEvent) => void`, `value: string`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components ButtonProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-button-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Button onPress={save}>Save</Button>
<Button variant="secondary" size="lg" onPress={cancel}>Cancel</Button>
<Button variant="danger" isLoading>Deleting…</Button>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/Button/Button.stories.tsx`, `packages/react/src/components/Dialog/Dialog.stories.tsx`, `packages/react/src/components/Tooltip/Tooltip.stories.tsx`

## Card

Import: `import { Card } from '@ds/react';`

Static, purely presentational surface container (a plain `<div>`, no role). Groups related content on a token-driven card surface. The ONLY sanctioned composition slots are `CardHeader`, `CardBody`, and `CardFooter` — there are no other slot components; layout inside a slot is plain HTML with space tokens.

Static component (no react-aria-components base) — plain semantic HTML.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `elevation` | `"flat" \| "raised"` | no | `'flat'` | Elevation treatment of the card surface. `flat` outlines the card with a border; `raised` lifts it with the card shadow (plus a hairline border under the shadow). |

Theming hooks: `--ds-card-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Card>
  <CardBody>Body-only card</CardBody>
</Card>
<Card elevation="raised">
  <CardHeader>
    <h3>Plan</h3>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardBody>Everything in Starter, plus unlimited seats.</CardBody>
  <CardFooter>
    <Button onPress={upgrade}>Upgrade</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/Card/Card.stories.tsx`

## Checkbox

Import: `import { Checkbox } from '@ds/react';`

Accessible checkbox built on react-aria-components `Checkbox`. The visible box is CSS-drawn over a visually hidden native input; the check and indeterminate marks are inline SVG stroked with `currentColor`. Keyboard behavior (Space toggles), focus management, and ARIA state come from React Aria; visual states are driven purely by RAC data attributes (`data-selected`, `data-indeterminate`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`) and `--ds-*` tokens.

Built on react-aria-components `Checkbox`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `Checkbox` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | no | — | Label content rendered next to the box. Always provide a visible label; the whole label is the click target. |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `defaultSelected` | `boolean` | no | — | Whether the checkbox is selected initially (uncontrolled). |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` | no | — | Disables the checkbox: interaction is blocked and the native input is disabled. |
| `isIndeterminate` | `boolean` | no | — | Marks the checkbox as indeterminate ("mixed"): a dash is shown instead of a check and assistive technology announces the mixed state. Typical for a "select all" control over a partially selected set. |
| `isInvalid` | `boolean` | no | — | Marks the checkbox as failing validation; the box takes the danger treatment and the state is exposed to assistive technology. |
| `isRequired` | `boolean` | no | — | Marks the checkbox as required before form submission. |
| `isSelected` | `boolean` | no | — | Whether the checkbox is selected (controlled). Pair with `onChange`. |
| `onChange` | `(isSelected: boolean) => void` | no | — | Handler called when the selection state changes. Receives the next selected state. |

Inherited-but-legal `Checkbox` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `autoFocus: boolean`, `isReadOnly: boolean`, `name: string`, `onPress: (e: PressEvent) => void`, `value: string`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components CheckboxProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-checkbox-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Checkbox onChange={setAccepted}>Accept terms</Checkbox>
<Checkbox isSelected={allSelected} isIndeterminate={someSelected} onChange={toggleAll}>
  Select all
</Checkbox>
<Checkbox isRequired isInvalid={showError}>I agree to the policy</Checkbox>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/Checkbox/Checkbox.stories.tsx`

## Dialog

Import: `import { Dialog } from '@ds/react';`

Modal dialog built on react-aria-components `DialogTrigger` + `Modal` + `Dialog`. Focus trapping, scroll locking, Escape/backdrop dismissal, and `aria-labelledby` wiring all come from React Aria; entry/exit states are driven by RAC data attributes (`data-entering`, `data-exiting`) with `--ds-motion-*` tokens, gated by `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Built on react-aria-components `Dialog`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `Dialog` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

Dialog OWNS its title: the required `title` prop renders the dialog's accessible heading with the system's own typography — never add your own heading element (`<h2>`, etc.) to name the dialog. Headings inside the dialog body are for content sections only.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes on the dialog panel. Narrowed to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | no | — | Whether the dialog is initially open (uncontrolled). |
| `isDismissable` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Whether the dialog can be dismissed by clicking the backdrop or pressing Escape. Set to `false` for flows that require an explicit choice; provide a closing action via the `children` render function's `close` callback. |
| `isOpen` | `boolean` | no | — | Whether the dialog is open (controlled). |
| `onOpenChange` | `(isOpen: boolean) => void` | no | — | Handler called when the dialog's open state changes (trigger pressed, Escape, backdrop click, or the `close` render-prop callback). |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | `'md'` | Width step of the dialog panel, applied as a `max-inline-size` cap; the panel shrinks to fit small viewports. |
| `title` | `string` | yes | — | Dialog title. Rendered as the react-aria-components `Heading` with `slot="title"`, which wires the dialog's `aria-labelledby` to it automatically. |
| `trigger` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` | no | — | Optional trigger element (e.g. a `Button`). When provided, the dialog is wrapped in a react-aria-components `DialogTrigger` and opens when the trigger is pressed. Omit it to control the dialog yourself via `isOpen`. |

Theming hooks: `--ds-dialog-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Dialog title="Delete project" trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete…</Button>}>
  {({ close }) => (
    <>
      <p>This action cannot be undone.</p>
      <Button variant="danger" onPress={close}>Confirm delete</Button>
    </>
  )}
</Dialog>

<Dialog title="Settings" size="lg" isOpen={isOpen} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <SettingsForm />
</Dialog>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/Dialog/Dialog.stories.tsx`

## IconButton

Import: `import { IconButton } from '@ds/react';`

Icon-only push button built on react-aria-components `Button`. A square control (width and height both from the button height scale) whose single child is a decorative icon; `aria-label` is required at the type level because it is the control's only accessible name. Keyboard behavior, focus management, and press semantics come from React Aria; visual states are driven purely by RAC data attributes (`data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`) and `--ds-*` tokens. Documented NR-008 exception (lead decision): IconButton belongs to the button family and consumes the `--ds-button-*` component-tier hook namespace rather than forking an `--ds-iconbutton-*` namespace of its own, so customer overrides of the button family restyle both controls together.

Built on react-aria-components `Button`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `Button` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` | `string` | yes | — | Accessible name for the button. Required at the type level: the icon is decorative (rendered `aria-hidden`), so this label is the ONLY accessible name the control has. There is no escape hatch. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | no | — | The icon to render. Presented to assistive technology as decorative (`aria-hidden`); the accessible name comes from `aria-label`. |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | no | `'md'` | Control size. The button is square: both dimensions come from the button height scale. |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost"` | no | `'ghost'` | Visual intent of the button. `ghost` is the low-emphasis default for toolbar/inline icon actions; `primary` is a main action, `secondary` a supporting action, `danger` a destructive action. |

Inherited-but-legal `Button` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `autoFocus: boolean`, `isDisabled: boolean`, `name: string`, `onPress: (e: PressEvent) => void`, `value: string`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components ButtonProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-button-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<IconButton aria-label="Close" onPress={close}>
  <CloseIcon />
</IconButton>
<IconButton aria-label="Add item" variant="primary" size="lg" onPress={add}>
  <PlusIcon />
</IconButton>
<IconButton aria-label="Delete row" variant="danger" onPress={remove}>
  <TrashIcon />
</IconButton>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/IconButton/IconButton.stories.tsx`

## Radio

Import: `import { Radio } from '@ds/react';`

A single option inside a `RadioGroup`, built on react-aria-components `Radio`. The circular control is drawn entirely in CSS (no icon assets) and reflects selection, hover, focus, invalid, and disabled states via RAC data attributes (`data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`).

Built on react-aria-components `Radio`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `Radio` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes | — | Label content rendered next to the CSS-drawn control. Required: every radio needs a visible accessible name. |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `value` | `string` | yes | — | Value this option contributes to the group: it is compared against the group's `value`/`defaultValue` and passed to the group's `onChange` when the option is selected. |

Inherited-but-legal `Radio` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `autoFocus: boolean`, `isDisabled: boolean`, `onPress: (e: PressEvent) => void`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components RadioProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-radio-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Radio value="email">Email</Radio>
<Radio value="sms" isDisabled>SMS</Radio>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/RadioGroup/RadioGroup.stories.tsx`

## RadioGroup

Import: `import { RadioGroup } from '@ds/react';`

A labeled group of mutually exclusive options built on react-aria-components `RadioGroup`. Roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation, and group labelling come from React Aria; visual states are driven purely by RAC data attributes (`data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-orientation`) and `--ds-*` tokens. Selection is single-value: `value`/`defaultValue` plus `onChange` receive the selected `Radio`'s `value` string.

Built on react-aria-components `RadioGroup`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `RadioGroup` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes | — | The `Radio` options of the group. |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `description` | `string` | no | — | Optional helper text rendered below the label and associated with the group via `aria-describedby`. |
| `errorMessage` | `string` | no | — | Error text rendered below the options. Only shown while the group is invalid (`isInvalid` or form validation); it is associated with the group via `aria-describedby`. |
| `label` | `string` | yes | — | Visible label naming the group. Required: a radio group without an accessible name is an accessibility failure, so the label is part of the typed contract rather than an optional slot. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | no | `'vertical'` | Layout axis of the options. `vertical` stacks the radios, `horizontal` lays them out in a wrapping row. Keyboard arrow navigation follows the orientation automatically via React Aria. |

Inherited-but-legal `RadioGroup` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `defaultValue: string \| null`, `isDisabled: boolean`, `isInvalid: boolean`, `isReadOnly: boolean`, `isRequired: boolean`, `name: string`, `onChange: (value: string) => void`, `value: string \| null`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components RadioGroupProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-radio-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<RadioGroup label="Notification method" onChange={setMethod}>
  <Radio value="email">Email</Radio>
  <Radio value="sms">SMS</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
<RadioGroup label="Density" orientation="horizontal" defaultValue="cozy">
  <Radio value="compact">Compact</Radio>
  <Radio value="cozy">Cozy</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
<RadioGroup label="Plan" isInvalid errorMessage="Choose a plan to continue.">
  <Radio value="free">Free</Radio>
  <Radio value="pro">Pro</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/RadioGroup/RadioGroup.stories.tsx`

## Select

Import: `import { Select } from '@ds/react';`

Accessible single-select built on react-aria-components `Select`, composing the RAC `Label`, `Button`, `SelectValue`, `Popover`, and `ListBox` parts internally behind a data-driven `items` API. Keyboard behavior (arrow keys, typeahead, Enter/Escape), focus management, and label/description/error wiring come from React Aria; visual states are driven purely by RAC data attributes (`data-open`, `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-focused`, `data-selected`) and `--ds-*` tokens. The trigger consumes the SHARED `--ds-field-*` token namespace — one override surface intentionally shared by TextField, TextArea, and Select so all form fields re-theme together.

Built on react-aria-components `Select`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `Select` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `defaultSelectedKey` | `string \| number \| null` | no | — | The `id` of the initially selected option (uncontrolled). |
| `description` | `string` | no | — | Help text rendered below the field and linked to the trigger via `aria-describedby`. |
| `errorMessage` | `string` | no | — | Error text rendered when the field is invalid (via `isInvalid` or failed native validation) and linked via `aria-describedby`. Hidden while the field is valid. |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Whether the field is disabled: the trigger cannot be focused or opened. |
| `isInvalid` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Whether the field value is invalid. Drives the error border, the `data-invalid` state, and rendering of `errorMessage`. |
| `isRequired` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Whether a selection is required before form submission. |
| `items` | `{ id: string \| number; label: string; isDisabled?: boolean; }[]` | yes | — | Typed options (v1 is a data-driven API, not free composition). Each option's `id` is the selection key and `label` is the visible and accessible text; `isDisabled` renders the option non-selectable. |
| `label` | `string` | yes | — | Visible field label. Required: the trigger's accessible name is derived from it, so a Select can never render unlabeled. |
| `onSelectionChange` | `(key: string \| number \| null) => void` | no | — | Handler called with the selected option's `id` (or `null`) when the selection changes. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | no | — | Text shown in the trigger while no option is selected. |
| `selectedKey` | `string \| number \| null` | no | — | The `id` of the currently selected option (controlled). `null` means no selection. |

Inherited-but-legal `Select` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `autoFocus: boolean`, `defaultOpen: boolean`, `isOpen: boolean`, `name: string`, `onOpenChange: (isOpen: boolean) => void`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components SelectProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-field-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Select
  label="Favorite fruit"
  placeholder="Pick a fruit"
  items={[
    { id: 'apple', label: 'Apple' },
    { id: 'banana', label: 'Banana' },
  ]}
  onSelectionChange={setFruit}
/>
<Select label="Plan" items={plans} selectedKey={plan} onSelectionChange={setPlan} isRequired />
<Select label="Region" items={regions} isInvalid errorMessage="Pick a region." />
```

## Switch

Import: `import { Switch } from '@ds/react';`

Accessible on/off switch built on react-aria-components `Switch`. The visible track and thumb are CSS-drawn over a visually hidden native input (`role="switch"`); the thumb slides with motion tokens and settles instantly under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Keyboard behavior (Space toggles), focus management, and ARIA state come from React Aria; visual states are driven purely by RAC data attributes (`data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`) and `--ds-*` tokens.

Built on react-aria-components `Switch`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `Switch` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | no | — | Label content rendered next to the track. Always provide a visible label; the whole label is the click target. |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `defaultSelected` | `boolean` | no | — | Whether the switch is on initially (uncontrolled). |
| `isDisabled` | `boolean` | no | — | Disables the switch: interaction is blocked and the native input is disabled. |
| `isSelected` | `boolean` | no | — | Whether the switch is on (controlled). Pair with `onChange`. |
| `onChange` | `(isSelected: boolean) => void` | no | — | Handler called when the on/off state changes. Receives the next selected state. |

Inherited-but-legal `Switch` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `autoFocus: boolean`, `isReadOnly: boolean`, `name: string`, `onPress: (e: PressEvent) => void`, `value: string`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components SwitchProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-switch-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Switch onChange={setNotifications}>Enable notifications</Switch>
<Switch isSelected={isDark} onChange={setIsDark}>Dark mode</Switch>
<Switch isDisabled>Beta features</Switch>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/Switch/Switch.stories.tsx`

## TabPanel

Import: `import { TabPanel } from '@ds/react';`

The content region for one tab, built on react-aria-components `TabPanel`. The `id` links it to the `Tab` with the same `id`; only the selected panel is mounted (pass `shouldForceMount` to keep it in the DOM). React Aria labels the panel from its tab and makes it focusable when it contains no focusable content.

Built on react-aria-components `TabPanel`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `TabPanel` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

## Tabs

Import: `import { Tabs } from '@ds/react';`

Container for a set of tabs, built on react-aria-components `Tabs`. Compose `TabList` (holding `Tab` triggers) with one `TabPanel` per tab; matching `id`s wire each trigger to its panel. Selection state, keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Home/End), and ARIA `tablist`/`tab`/`tabpanel` wiring all come from React Aria; visual states are driven purely by RAC data attributes (`data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`) and `--ds-*` tokens. Horizontal only in v1.

Built on react-aria-components `Tabs`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `Tabs` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |

Inherited-but-legal `Tabs` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `defaultSelectedKey: Key`, `isDisabled: boolean`, `onSelectionChange: (key: Key) => void`, `selectedKey: Key`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components TabsProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-tabs-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Tabs defaultSelectedKey="overview">
  <TabList aria-label="Project sections">
    <Tab id="overview">Overview</Tab>

</Tabs>
```

## TextArea

Import: `import { TextArea } from '@ds/react';`

Accessible multi-line text input built on react-aria-components `TextField` with a `TextArea` element. Label, description, and error wiring (`aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`) come from React Aria; visual states are driven purely by RAC data attributes (`data-hovered`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`) and `--ds-*` tokens. Styling consumes the SHARED `--ds-field-*` hook namespace — by design, TextField, TextArea, and Select theme together as one field surface.

Built on react-aria-components `TextField`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `TextField` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `autoGrow` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Grow the field with its content instead of scrolling. Implemented with CSS `field-sizing: content` (no JS, no dependencies); browsers without support fall back to the fixed `rows` height with a scrollbar. Manual resize is disabled while auto-growing. |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `description` | `string` | no | — | Optional help text rendered below the field and linked to the textarea via `aria-describedby`. |
| `errorMessage` | `string` | no | — | Error text rendered when the field is invalid (via `isInvalid` or a failed `validate`). When omitted, react-aria-components' built-in validation messages are shown instead. |
| `label` | `string` | yes | — | Visible label for the field. Always rendered and associated with the textarea for assistive technology — there is no unlabeled variant. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | no | — | Temporary hint text shown while the field is empty. Never a substitute for `label`. |
| `rows` | `number` | no | `3` | Initial visible text rows. With `autoGrow`, serves as the fallback height in browsers without `field-sizing` support. |

Inherited-but-legal `TextField` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `autoFocus: boolean`, `defaultValue: string \| null`, `isDisabled: boolean`, `isInvalid: boolean`, `isReadOnly: boolean`, `isRequired: boolean`, `name: string`, `onChange: (value: string) => void`, `value: string \| null`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components TextFieldProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-field-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<TextArea label="Message" placeholder="Tell us more…" />
<TextArea label="Notes" description="Visible to the whole team." rows={5} />
<TextArea label="Feedback" autoGrow isRequired isInvalid errorMessage="Feedback is required." />
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/TextArea/TextArea.stories.tsx`

## TextField

Import: `import { TextField } from '@ds/react';`

Accessible single-line text input built on react-aria-components `TextField`, composing RAC `Label`, `Input`, `Text` (description), and `FieldError` internally — label association, description/error wiring (`aria-describedby`), and invalid-state announcement come from React Aria. Validation and state flow through the RAC props (`isInvalid`, `isRequired`, `isDisabled`, `value`/`defaultValue`/`onChange`, `type`, `name`, ...). The forwarded `ref` reaches the underlying `<input>`. Styling consumes the `--ds-field-*` component-token namespace, which is SHARED by TextField, TextArea, and Select by design: one customer override retunes every form field consistently.

Built on react-aria-components `TextField`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `TextField` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes on the field root. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `description` | `string` | no | — | Optional helper text rendered below the input as a RAC `Text` with `slot="description"`, linked to the input via `aria-describedby`. |
| `errorMessage` | `string` | no | — | Error text rendered in a RAC `FieldError` below the input. It is only shown while the field is invalid (`isInvalid` or failed validation) and is linked to the input via `aria-describedby`. |
| `label` | `string` | yes | — | Visible label for the field. Required: the label is rendered as a RAC `Label` and associated with the input automatically, so the field is always accessibly named. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | no | — | Placeholder text shown inside the input while it is empty. Forwarded to the inner RAC `Input` (react-aria-components moves `placeholder` off the `TextField` root). Not a substitute for `label`. |

Inherited-but-legal `TextField` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `autoFocus: boolean`, `defaultValue: string \| null`, `isDisabled: boolean`, `isInvalid: boolean`, `isReadOnly: boolean`, `isRequired: boolean`, `name: string`, `onChange: (value: string) => void`, `value: string \| null`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components TextFieldProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-field-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<TextField label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
<TextField
  label="Display name"
  description="Shown on your public profile."
/>
<TextField
  label="Email"
  isRequired
  isInvalid
  errorMessage="Enter a valid email address."
/>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/TextField/TextField.stories.tsx`

## Tooltip

Import: `import { Tooltip } from '@ds/react';`

Contextual text label shown near a trigger element on hover or keyboard focus, built on react-aria-components `TooltipTrigger` + `Tooltip`. Open/close timing, positioning, flipping, and the `role="tooltip"` / `aria-describedby` wiring come from React Aria; visuals are driven purely by RAC data attributes (`data-placement`, `data-entering`, `data-exiting`) and `--ds-*` tokens (inverse-surface recipe via the `--ds-tooltip-*` hooks). Content is plain text only — tooltips never hold interactive content.

Built on react-aria-components `Tooltip`; keyboard behavior, ARIA, and focus management ship inside. All `Tooltip` base props (e.g. event handlers, `isDisabled`, `autoFocus`) are also legal here, with the props listed below overriding or narrowing them.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` | yes | — | The trigger element the tooltip describes. Must be a focusable, hoverable element (e.g. `Button`) — React Aria attaches hover *and* focus triggering to it, which keyboard accessibility requires. |
| `className` | `string` | no | — | Additional CSS class appended after the component's own classes. Narrowed from the react-aria-components render-prop form to a plain string; inline `style` is intentionally not supported (token rule). |
| `content` | `string` | yes | — | Text shown inside the tooltip bubble. Deliberately typed as `string`, not `ReactNode`: a tooltip vanishes as soon as pointer or focus leaves its trigger, so links, buttons, or any other interactive content inside it could never be reached by keyboard or assistive technology. The type forbids that class of misuse at compile time. |
| `delay` | `number` | no | `1500` | Warmup delay in milliseconds before the tooltip shows on hover. Showing on keyboard focus is always immediate. The default is the react-aria warmup delay (no dedicated motion token exists for tooltip delay in the current token set). |
| `placement` | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | no | `'top'` | Which side of the trigger the tooltip appears on. Automatically flips to the opposite side when there is not enough room in the viewport. |

Inherited-but-legal `Tooltip` props (from the registry `racProps` enumeration): `defaultOpen: boolean`, `isOpen: boolean`, `onOpenChange: (isOpen: boolean) => void`. Commonly needed props inherited from the react-aria-components base; the full react-aria-components TooltipProps surface is also legal.

Theming hooks: `--ds-tooltip-*` component-tier tokens (see registries/tokens-index.json); they belong to this component ONLY (NR-008).

@example
```tsx
<Tooltip content="Save your changes">
  <Button onPress={save}>Save</Button>
</Tooltip>
<Tooltip content="Delete project" placement="bottom" delay={500}>
  <Button variant="ghost" aria-label="Delete">🗑</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

Ground-truth stories: `packages/react/src/components/Tooltip/Tooltip.stories.tsx`

# Design System — tokens (brand: acme)
> GENERATED by @ds/context — DO NOT EDIT. Source hash sha256:40eab412d89cd909. Regenerate: pnpm --filter @ds/context build

This system is closed-world: every legal component is enumerated in registries/components-index.json and every legal token in registries/tokens-index.json. Anything not in those registries is provably fabricated — do not emit it.

232 tokens. Values below are RESOLVED for the `acme` brand (source: brands/acme.json); a different brand build re-emits this file with its own values. Reference tokens only as `var(--ds-…)` — never paste resolved values into code.

Tier rules: semantic tokens (intent-named) are the general vocabulary; component tokens (`--ds-<component>-*`) are theming hooks that belong to their component ONLY — never borrow another component's hooks. Space tokens are legal only in margin/padding/gap/inset; box dimensions use `--ds-size-*`.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `border.width.1` | `--ds-border-width-1` | `1px` | Standard border width for inputs, cards, and separators. |
| `border.width.2` | `--ds-border-width-2` | `2px` | Emphasized border width for focus indicators and selected states. |

| `color.surface.raised` | `--ds-color-surface-raised` | `#fef9f6` | Background for content lifted above the page — cards, menus, popovers, dialogs. Pair with shadow.raised or shadow.overlay. |
| `color.surface.sunken` | `--ds-color-surface-sunken` | `#ede6e1` | Recessed background for wells, inset panels, code blocks, and zebra stripes that sit visually below the default surface. |
| `color.surface.sunken-hover` | `--ds-color-surface-sunken-hover` | `#dad2cd` | Hover/pressed step for interactive sunken surfaces, e.g. the Switch off-state track under the pointer. One ramp step darker than color.surface.sunken; not a text background. |
| `color.text.inverse` | `--ds-color-text-inverse` | `#fef9f6` | Text used on color.surface.inverse and other dark regions such as tooltips. |
| `color.text.link` | `--ds-color-text-link` | `#1e6e4a` | Inline hyperlink color; AA-checked on default, raised, and sunken surfaces. |
| `color.text.muted` | `--ds-color-text-muted` | `#59534e` | De-emphasized text for placeholders, hints, and metadata. The lightest text color that remains AA on all light surfaces. |
| `color.text.on-accent` | `--ds-color-text-on-accent` | `#fef9f6` | Text and icon color for accent-filled controls; AA-checked against color.accent.default and color.accent.emphasis. |
| `color.text.primary` | `--ds-color-text-primary` | `#1c1713` | Primary reading color for body copy and headings on default, raised, and sunken surfaces. |
| `color.text.secondary` | `--ds-color-text-secondary` | `#453f3a` | Supporting text — descriptions, captions, secondary labels. Lower emphasis than primary while staying AA on all light surfaces. |

### motion (6)

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Description |

| `motion.duration.slow` | `--ds-motion-duration-slow` | `320ms` | Large-surface transitions: dialogs, drawers, page-level changes. |

| `motion.easing.exit` | `--ds-motion-easing-exit` | `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)` | Accelerating easing for elements leaving the screen. |
| `motion.easing.standard` | `--ds-motion-easing-standard` | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | Default easing for on-screen state changes; starts and ends gently. |

### size (9)

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size.container.lg` | `--ds-size-container-lg` | `calc(40px * 30)` | Maximum inline size of wide page shells: multi-column dashboards, full-width app frames (30x the md control height / derived.space.8; 1200px at the default brand). Use this — never a space token or a raw calc — for content column widths (NR-006). |
| `size.container.md` | `--ds-size-container-md` | `calc(40px * 24)` | Maximum inline size of standard content columns: list pages, dashboards with a single column (24x the md control height / derived.space.8; 960px at the default brand). Use this — never a space token or a raw calc — for content column widths (NR-006). |
| `size.container.sm` | `--ds-size-container-sm` | `calc(40px * 16)` | Maximum inline size of narrow content columns: settings pages, forms, prose (16x the md control height / derived.space.8; 640px at the default brand). Matches the lg dialog width derivation. Use this — never a space token or a raw calc — for content column widths (NR-006). |
| `size.control.lg` | `--ds-size-control-lg` | `48px` | Height of large interactive controls for prominent actions (12x the brand space base). |
| `size.control.md` | `--ds-size-control-md` | `40px` | Default height of interactive controls: buttons, inputs, and selects (10x the brand space base). |
| `size.control.sm` | `--ds-size-control-sm` | `32px` | Height of small interactive controls: compact buttons, inputs, and selects (8x the brand space base). |
| `size.icon.lg` | `--ds-size-icon-lg` | `24px` | Icon and spinner size for prominent controls, empty states, and alerts (6x the brand space base). Use this — never a space token — to size an element. |
| `size.icon.md` | `--ds-size-icon-md` | `20px` | Default icon and spinner size alongside body text and inside md controls (5x the brand space base). Use this — never a space token — to size an element. |
| `size.icon.sm` | `--ds-size-icon-sm` | `16px` | Icon and spinner size inside compact controls and dense UI (4x the brand space base). Use this — never a space token — to size an element. |

### space (17)

| `space.10` | `--ds-space-10` | `64px` | Space step 10 (16x the brand space base); the largest layout separation. |
| `space.2` | `--ds-space-2` | `8px` | Space step 2 (2x the brand space base); compact padding and small gaps. |
| `space.3` | `--ds-space-3` | `12px` | Space step 3 (3x the brand space base); default control padding. |
| `space.4` | `--ds-space-4` | `16px` | Space step 4 (4x the brand space base); default gap between related elements. |
| `space.5` | `--ds-space-5` | `20px` | Space step 5 (5x the brand space base); padding for medium containers. |
| `space.6` | `--ds-space-6` | `24px` | Space step 6 (6x the brand space base); padding for large containers and section gaps. |
| `space.7` | `--ds-space-7` | `32px` | Space step 7 (8x the brand space base); separation between content groups. |
| `space.8` | `--ds-space-8` | `40px` | Space step 8 (10x the brand space base); separation between major regions. |
| `space.9` | `--ds-space-9` | `48px` | Space step 9 (12x the brand space base); large layout separation. |
| `space.gap.lg` | `--ds-space-gap-lg` | `16px` | Large flex/grid gap between loosely related groups (4x the brand space base). |
| `space.gap.md` | `--ds-space-gap-md` | `8px` | Default flex/grid gap between sibling elements (2x the brand space base). |
| `space.gap.sm` | `--ds-space-gap-sm` | `4px` | Small flex/grid gap for tightly related items (1x the brand space base). |
| `space.inset.lg` | `--ds-space-inset-lg` | `24px` | Generous uniform internal padding for large containers (6x the brand space base). |
| `space.inset.md` | `--ds-space-inset-md` | `16px` | Default uniform internal padding for containers (4x the brand space base). |
| `space.inset.sm` | `--ds-space-inset-sm` | `8px` | Small uniform internal padding for compact containers (2x the brand space base). |

| `text.weight.semibold` | `--ds-text-weight-semibold` | `600` | Headings and strong inline emphasis. |

| `radio.dot` | `--ds-radio-dot` | `#f9f3ef` | Color of the inset dot ring punched into the selected radio fill. |
| `radio.gap` | `--ds-radio-gap` | `4px` | Gap between the radio control circle and its label. |
| `radio.size` | `--ds-radio-size` | `20px` | Diameter of the radio control circle. |
| `radio.surface.selected` | `--ds-radio-surface-selected` | `#28825a` | Fill and border of the selected radio control; the dot is punched into this fill. |
| `radio.surface.selected-hover` | `--ds-radio-surface-selected-hover` | `#1e6e4a` | Fill and border of the selected radio control on hover and while pressed. |

### switch (7)

| Token | CSS variable | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `switch.surface.off` | `--ds-switch-surface-off` | `#ede6e1` | Track fill when the switch is off; hover uses color.surface.sunken-hover. |
| `switch.surface.on` | `--ds-switch-surface-on` | `#28825a` | Track fill when the switch is on. |
| `switch.surface.on-hover` | `--ds-switch-surface-on-hover` | `#1e6e4a` | Track fill when the switch is on and hovered or pressed. |
| `switch.thumb` | `--ds-switch-thumb` | `#f9f3ef` | Thumb fill in the off state; the on state switches to color.text.on-accent so the thumb stays visible on the accent track. |
| `switch.thumb-size` | `--ds-switch-thumb-size` | `16px` | Diameter of the switch thumb. |
| `switch.track-height` | `--ds-switch-track-height` | `20px` | Block size of the switch track; also sets the thumb inset via calc in CSS. |
| `switch.track-width` | `--ds-switch-track-width` | `calc(20px * 2)` | Inline size of the switch track (2x the md icon size; 40px at the default brand). The thumb slide distance is track-width minus track-height, derived in CSS. |

# Design System — theming (brand: acme)
> GENERATED by @ds/context — DO NOT EDIT. Source hash sha256:40eab412d89cd909. Regenerate: pnpm --filter @ds/context build

White-labeling is a token-and-pipeline problem, not a component problem. A customer theme is a data file, never a fork.

## The three-tier token model

1. **Brand tier** (`brands/<name>.json`) — raw values only: palette ramps (`palette.{neutral,primary,…}.{50…950}`), typefaces, type scale (base + ratio), radius scale, space base, elevation, logo assets. This is the ONLY tier a customer theme may replace.
2. **Semantic tier** (`--ds-{category}-{concept}[-{variant}][-{state}]`) — intent-named mappings onto brand ramp positions (`--ds-color-surface-raised`, never `--ds-blue-500`). Usage sites reference this tier. Customers do not edit mappings; semantic overrides are a separate, allowlisted layer.
3. **Component tier** (`--ds-<component>-*`) — per-component hooks consumed by that component's CSS. The per-component customer override surface.

Gap vs space steps: the `--ds-space-gap-{sm,md,lg}` trio (tops out at `gap-lg`) is for intra-component rhythm (icon-to-label, control clusters, sibling gaps); larger section- and region-level separation uses the plain space steps (`--ds-space-5` and up).

## Brand-file mechanics

A customer engagement produces one `brands/<customer>.json` in the same shape as the neutral core (`brands/default.json`): raw ramps, no intent. The pipeline then rebuilds everything: tokens-build resolves semantic + component tiers against the brand file, validates EVERY color mapping for WCAG 2.2 AA contrast (current brand: 0 failures across 27 audited pairs), regenerates the registries, and re-runs this context compiler with `--brand <customer>` so llms.txt, docs, skills, editor rules, and the auditor agent all reflect the customer's resolved values. Zero component code changes for standard engagements.

## Allowlisted extension points (everything else is closed)

Machine contract: `extension-points.json` in this bundle (ADR-006) — the authoritative allowlist.

1. **Brand-tier token file** — replace raw ramp values wholesale.
2. **Semantic overrides** — a separate, explicitly-allowlisted override layer applied at intake (contrast-validated like everything else).
3. **Component-tier hooks** — override per-component custom properties:
- `--ds-alert-*` — 22 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
- `--ds-badge-*` — 15 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
- `--ds-button-*` — 21 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
- `--ds-card-*` — 6 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
- `--ds-checkbox-*` — 8 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
- `--ds-dialog-*` — 11 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
- `--ds-field-*` — 18 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
- `--ds-radio-*` — 5 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
- `--ds-switch-*` — 7 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
- `--ds-tabs-*` — 9 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
- `--ds-tooltip-*` — 9 hooks (see llms-tokens.txt for the exact list)
4. **Composition + `className`** — every component accepts a plain-string `className` appended after its own classes; compose components and plain elements for layout.

## Not extension points (negative rules apply)

- Semantic-tier intent mappings (customer files replace values, never mappings).
- Component CSS or component source — never fork.
- Raw palette scales at usage sites (`--ds-blue-500` does not exist publicly).
- Another component's hooks (overriding Alert must never restyle Badge).
- Inline `style` props — intentionally not supported; use tokens in CSS.


# Design System — migration (brand: acme)
> GENERATED by @ds/context — DO NOT EDIT. Source hash sha256:40eab412d89cd909. Regenerate: pnpm --filter @ds/context build

> Your training data about this design system is stale or empty. This system is closed-world: if a component or token is not in the registry, it does not exist. Do not adapt patterns from Chakra, MUI, Ant, or shadcn.

This slice maps habits from raw HTML/CSS, Tailwind, and other design systems onto this system. It is compiled from the living negative-rule catalog — every rule below was observed or anticipated as a real agent hallucination.

## From Tailwind / utility CSS

- Utility classes are not part of this system: replace `className="p-4 rounded-lg text-gray-600"` with a CSS Module class consuming tokens (`padding: var(--ds-space-4); border-radius: var(--ds-radius-lg); color: var(--ds-color-text-muted);`).
- Tailwind's spacing-scale-for-everything habit does not transfer: space tokens are only legal in margin/padding/gap/inset; widths and heights use `--ds-size-*` (e.g. `--ds-size-control-md`).
- Color utilities map to intent tokens, not hue scales: `text-gray-600` → `var(--ds-color-text-secondary)` or `-muted` by intent, never a raw scale.

## From Chakra / MUI / Ant / shadcn

- Layout primitives (`Box`, `Stack`, `Container`, `Flex`, `Grid`, `Spacer`) and typography components (`Heading`, `Text`) do not exist here — intentionally. Use plain semantic HTML plus CSS with tokens. (Exception to hand-rolled headings: Dialog renders its own title from its required `title` prop — never add a heading element to name a dialog.)
- Theme-object styling (`sx`, `css` props, styled()) does not exist; components accept `className` only, and inline `style` is intentionally unsupported.
- Import from the single entry point `@ds/react`; deep dist paths are not public API.

## From raw HTML / hand-rolled CSS

- Replace hex/rgb literals with intent tokens; the validator rejects hard-coded values in component CSS.
- Replace `:hover`/`:focus-visible`/`:disabled` pseudo-classes with react-aria data attributes (`[data-hovered]`, `[data-focus-visible]`, `[data-disabled]`) when styling this system's components.
- Do not hand-roll focus traps, keyboard navigation, or ARIA — the components ship it (react-aria-components).

## The negative-rule catalog (wrong → right)

### NR-001 Layout primitives do not exist
- Wrong: `<Box p={4}>`, `<Stack gap="md">`, `<Container>`, `<Flex>`, `<Grid>`, `<Spacer>`
- Right: plain elements + CSS with space tokens: `display:flex; gap: var(--ds-space-gap-md)`
- Why: most-hallucinated components industry-wide; intentionally not shipped.

### NR-002 Typography components do not exist
- Wrong: `<Heading level={2}>`, `<Text size="sm">`
- Right: semantic HTML (`<h2>`, `<p>`) with `var(--ds-text-size-*)` / `var(--ds-text-weight-*)`

### NR-003 Raw color scales are not public tokens
- Wrong: `var(--ds-blue-500)`, `var(--ds-palette-primary-600)`, hex literals
- Right: intent tokens: `var(--ds-color-accent-default)`, `var(--ds-color-text-primary)`

### NR-004 Tailwind/utility classes are not part of this system
- Wrong: `className="p-4 rounded-lg text-gray-600"`
- Right: CSS Module class consuming `--ds-*` tokens

### NR-005 Do not import from deep paths
- Wrong: `import Button from '@ds/react/dist/Button'`
- Right: `import { Button } from '@ds/react'` — the only public entry point

### NR-006 Space tokens are not sizes
- Wrong: `inline-size: var(--ds-space-4)`, `height: var(--ds-space-6)`
- Right: size tokens for boxes: `var(--ds-size-control-md)`, `var(--ds-size-icon-md)`; space tokens only in margin/padding/gap/inset
- Why: spacing scales pattern-match to sizing in Tailwind-trained output; breaks independently-themable density.

### NR-007 There is no `on-status` text token
- Wrong: `var(--ds-color-text-on-danger)`, `var(--ds-color-status-danger-on)`
- Right: `var(--ds-color-text-inverse)` on solid status fills — and only pairs present in registries/contrast-report.json
- Why: `on-accent` exists, so agents extrapolate `on-<anything>`; the extrapolated names are fabricated.

### NR-008 Component-tier tokens belong to their component only
- Wrong: `background: var(--ds-alert-surface-info)` inside Badge.module.css
- Right: Badge uses `--ds-badge-*` or semantic-tier tokens
- Why: cross-component borrowing couples theming hooks; overriding Alert would silently restyle Badge.

### NR-009 State selectors are RAC data attributes, not pseudo-classes
- Wrong: `.button:hover`, `.tab:focus-visible`, `.field input:disabled`
- Right: `.button[data-hovered]`, `.tab[data-focus-visible]`, `[data-disabled]`
- Why: pseudo-classes fire on touch emulation and on disabled elements; react-aria-components normalizes interaction state.

### NR-010 The base class is the lowercased component name
- Wrong: `.root`, `.wrapper`, `.container` as the component's base CSS class
- Right: `.button`, `.card`, `.alert` — composed as `[styles.<name>, styles[variant], styles[size], className]`
- Why: one canon keeps tests and docgen grep-stable across 14 components.

## Migration workflow

1. Enumerate the closed world: read `registries/components-index.json` and `registries/tokens-index.json` (or llms-components.txt / llms-tokens.txt).
2. Map each legacy element/class to a registry component or to plain HTML + tokens, using the pairs above.
3. Port screen by screen; never carry over utility classes, inline styles, or fabricated components.
4. Gate every ported screen on the deterministic gauntlet: `pnpm validate` (typecheck → lint → build → test/a11y → registry check).
